answer: Identity issuance is priced by cohort. Each epoch the protocol counts keys registered in it, charging each a bond scaled to that count squared, so a solo entrant pays a rounding error, a farm minting ten thousand keys at once a hundred million times more. The charge enters the same quartz ledger as attestations, public before any key votes, and unlocks after a hundred closed epochs, outliving any puppet. Sponsorship is the second brake: an established backer grafts a newcomer onto its reputation vine, and one upheld fraud verdict burns the graft to the root. Together they form a price spiral.
